sources.title: Functional Errata / Relevant Functional Errata - EdisonFormat.com
sources.used_for: The Edison community's explicit per-card list of cards errata'd after 2010 whose 2010-era behaviour differs from the modern text, plus the period rulings corpus (Individual Card Rulings posts) documenting the era's failed-search Deck/hand verification card by card. Used as independent corroboration of functional/ruling classifications - e.g. Sangan (the searched monster's effects were usable), Rescue Cat (no negation, no once-per-name), Catapult Turtle / Brionac / Treeborn Frog / Destiny End Dragoon (no once-per-turn), Necrovalley (negation applied only to effects targeting in a Graveyard), Darkness Approaches (face-down ATTACK position), Goyo Guardian (non-EARTH Tuners legal as material), Union monsters (the one-Union-per-monster Condition, removed by later errata).
sources.reliability_notes: Community secondary source; the blog version (2020-07-01) cites Konami tournament-policy section IX.G as the reason post-2010 errata text governs sanctioned play, which is why the site documents the era behaviour separately. It corroborates behaviour, not chronology: the page dates nothing, so effective dates are anchored to printings or to primary rulings documents instead.

sources.title: Konami TCG Strategy Site errata announcement articles and Forbidden & Limited List pages (archived)
sources.notes: Konami's own announcements of TCG functional errata, plus the archived F/L list pages that carry an explicit 'Effective from <date>' and 'UPDATED: <date>'. Two announced waves cover most of the modern errata in this corpus: 2015-03-20 (effective 2015-04-01) for Sinister Serpent, Ring of Destruction, Crush Card Virus and Exchange of the Spirit - 'the text of 5 Forbidden cards has been altered, and they will become Limited cards on April 1st'; and 2017-03-27 (effective 2017-03-31, the Duelist Saga wave) for Rescue Cat, Imperial Order, Brain Control, Future Fusion, Goyo Guardian and Brionac. Konami's own CURRENT CARD ERRATA LIST PDFs (2009-07-30, 2010-01-05, 2010-11-05) and the Konami EU 'Errata Cards' page corroborate several others, and state the governing doctrine: 'If a card has errata, you should always play the card as if it had the corrected text.' Used to upgrade printing-derived dates from reported to verified; the printing remains the date anchor because it is when the text first became available in the TCG. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Upper Deck Entertainment official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings pages (Internet Archive captures, 2005-2009)
sources.notes: UDE's per-card rulings database, the ruling layer in force in the GOAT era. The 2005-06-16 capture (inside the April-October 2005 GOAT window) states the failed-search verification procedure verbatim for Sangan and Witch of the Black Forest: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify.' Reinforcement of the Army's entry then permitted activation with no valid target subject to the same verification; by the 2008-12-15 yugioh-card.com Card FAQ capture that had changed to 'You cannot activate ... if you do not have any Level 4 or lower Warrior-Type monsters remaining in your Deck' - per-card activation-condition chronology differs from the shared verification chronology. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Konami per-set Card Rulings documents, 2010-2011 (yugioh-card.com, Internet Archive)
sources.notes: Konami's official rulings documents for the Konami era. 'Machina Mayhem Structure Deck - Card Rulings, Compiled as of April 6th, 2010' - eighteen days before the Edison snapshot - applies failed-search verification twice ('If you do not have "Commander Covington" in your Deck, your opponent can ask to verify'). Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16) extends it to the Extra Deck and Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02) to the hand; 2011-02-02 is the latest date the old state is positively attested. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Konami Digital Entertainment Official Tournament Policy - 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' (archived, 2019-2025)
sources.notes: The modern state: KDE tournament policy forbids searching or verifying an opponent's Deck outside specific cases, using a failed Mystic Tomato search as its worked example. First located capture 2019-04-03; unchanged in KDE-US Tournament Policy v2.5 (in effect 2025-09-05). The KDE policy documents in force in April 2010 (Tournament Policy v1.0 valid 2010-02-01, Penalty Guidelines valid 2010-04-01) contain no failure-to-find clause at all - in that era the rule lived in the rulings layer, not policy. No dated announcement of the change was found: the transition interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 remains open. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Format Library source repository (danielmcnelis/formatlibrary)
sources.notes: Nx monorepo behind formatlibrary.com. Inspected for its errata data model: libs/models/src/lib/Errata.js defines an 'erratas' table (cardName, cardId, description, effectiveDate, expirationDate, isOriginal, isActive) that no route, script or UI reads - schema-only. Period card texts actually live per printing in Print.description (populated by a Feb 2024 Yugipedia scrape) and are deliberately excluded from the card API response; the site-wide Card.description is the CURRENT text synced nightly from YGOPRODeck. Format-specific behaviour is carried by human-written Ruling rows keyed to a format, not by machine-readable period text. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Upper Deck Entertainment 'Card Text Updates / Errata & Card Text FAQ's' page (Internet Archive captures)
sources.notes: UDE's official running list of TCG card-text corrections and updated texts, per card with the affected printings. A capture attests the OFFICIAL text as of the capture date, which bounds text-change chronology in the UDE era; Yugipedia's Card Errata pages cite this page for several UDE-announced errata (e.g. the XYZ union monsters). Local copy of the 2009-02-20 capture in the research cache; retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Yugipedia Card Errata pages (Card Errata: namespace, per-language {{Errata table}} text lineages)
sources.notes: One structured page per errata'd card: successive card texts with diff markup, each captioned with the printing (set + number) exemplifying that version. Fetched via the MediaWiki API by retroformats/importers/fetch_errata_sources.py (batched revisions queries, 1 req/s, descriptive UA); page revision ids are stamped into the research packets. Used for text lineages and for bounding when a new text was first available in the TCG (the introducing printing's set release date); wording is community-transcribed, so functional-vs-cosmetic judgements also cross-check the pinned BabelCDB texts.

sources.title: Yugipedia set pages (Semantic MediaWiki release-date properties, per territory)
sources.notes: Queried per the published API policy (1 req/s, descriptive UA, cached). Exact queries, retrieval dates, and page counts are stamped into data/imported/releases-report.json by the importer. Date precision parsed from SMW raw values (1/YYYY[/M[/D]]), never from padded timestamps.

sources.title: Konami "OFFICIAL RULEBOOK Version 7.1" (archived 2010-03-30, 25 days before SJC Edison)
sources.notes: The general TCG rulebook current at Edison. Defines Ignition Effects as usable "just by declaring its activation during your Main Phase" and describes the general "Turn Player's Priority" rule (no card/effect activation while the turn player holds it) - this general prose is genuinely ambiguous on its own about whether the special immediate "Ignition Effect Priority" window (see docs/research/edison-rules.md #1) applies after any chain resolution or only after a Summon; period forum sources, not this rulebook text, resolve that question. States the ATK-tie battle rule ("both monsters are destroyed") with no 0-ATK exception. Text verbatim-identical to the Dec-2008 V7.0 capture and the Nov-2011 V8.0 capture (which already includes Xyz Monsters), so this document brackets Edison on both sides. Retrieved 2026-08-21.

sources.title: Konami "Official Rulebook" Version 7.0 (archived 2008-12-30)
sources.notes: Earlier bracket for the V7.1 (2010) rulebook comparison: confirms Ignition Effect/Priority wording and the ATK-tie battle rule were already the same 16 months before Edison, not a recent change.

sources.title: Konami "OFFICIAL RULEBOOK Version 7.2" (packaged with Structure Deck: Dragunity Legion, TCG release ~2011-03-04/08; archived on the general rulebook download page 2011-05-16)
sources.notes: Adds the explicit "0 ATK monsters... neither monster is destroyed" exception (p.43), absent from V7.1/V7.0 - dates the 0-ATK-tie-destroys-both-to-0-ATK-tie-destroys-neither change to on or shortly before the Dragunity Legion Structure Deck's TCG street date (~10.5 months after Edison), not May 2011: the PDF's own embedded metadata (title "3R03450 - SD Dragunity Rulebook EN.pdf", CreationDate 2011-03-04) and cover text ("OFFICIAL RULEBOOK Version 7.2") confirm it is the same document Konami and community sources both call "Version 7.2", not a later "New Master Rules" edition (that name does not appear in this file or Konami's rulebook index page at any point in the archived history checked); the 2011-05-16 Wayback capture is simply when this already-released PDF was captured on the general public download page. Priority/Ignition-Effect prose is otherwise unchanged from the 2008/2010 editions. Corrected 2026-08-21 from an earlier, mislabeled "New Master Rules" / "13 months after Edison" citation - see docs/research/edison-rules.md #6 for the correction record.

sources.title: Konami "Fast Effect Timing" flowchart page (earliest capture 2012-04-27)
sources.notes: The page EdisonFormat.com cites as its baseline for Ignition Effect Priority - but its earliest archive capture is two days after the TCG adopted the narrower OCG-style ignition condition (2012-04-25), i.e. it postdates Edison by two years and documents the era AFTER the one it is cited for. Not evidence of April 2010 TCG procedure by itself.

sources.title: Average Duelist blog, "Rulebook Update: Fast Effects and Priority" (2012-04-25)
sources.notes: Contemporaneous (dated the day of the change) community report that the TCG adopted the OCG's narrower ignition-priority ruling on 2012-04-25, explicitly confirming TCG and OCG differed on this point before that date - the change is two years after Edison.

sources.title: EdisonFormat.com, "What is Priority?" (/priority.html)
sources.notes: The community's own formalization of "Ignition Effect Priority" for Edison, explicitly stated to be the community's OWN ADDITION on top of Konami's (much later, 2012-era) fast-effect-timing flowchart - a lead, not itself period evidence. Its narrower framing (Summon-response-only) is a pedagogical simplification; the period rulebook text (konami-official-rulebook-v71-2010) is broader.

sources.title: Konami "Advanced Gameplay FAQ" page, section "Simultaneous Effects" (archived 2008-12-15 / 2009-01-05)
sources.notes: Official FAQ (not the rulebook booklet) describing SEGOC as a simple two-tier system - turn player's simultaneous Trigger Effects first (freely ordered), then the opponent's - citing "pages 35-37 of the Official Rulebook version 6.0", which pushes this rule's attested pedigree back to ~2007/08. No mandatory-before-optional split or trigger-order tiebreak appears in this text. Worked example given: Mystic Tomato vs. Mystic Tomato.

sources.title: Pojo.com Forums, "Rulings FAQ: PLEASE READ BEFORE POSTING!" post by gateguardian44 (2009-04-16)
sources.notes: Dated a full year before Edison, explicitly citing 'Pgs. 34-36 of the rulebook (ver. 7.0)' and laying out a 7-Substep Damage Step structure essentially identical, sub-step for sub-step, to what edisonformat.com/.net present today as Edison's '7-timing Damage Step'. Period-adjacent secondary evidence that the finer (non-GOAT-'6-step') Damage Step structure was already in place at least a year before Edison; the exact 2005-to-2009 transition date remains unknown.

sources.title: DuelistGroundz "OCG Land" forum thread, "SEGOC in Japan" (posted 2012-06-26 through 2012-06-29)
sources.notes: Two posters (ness00, AEtherchild) claim the four-tier mandatory-before-optional SEGOC structure with an earlier-trigger tiebreak was already unwritten TCG tournament-floor practice 'for years' before 2012, contradicting the period-primary Official Rulebook text (unchanged 2008-2011, konami-official-rulebook-v71-2010) which describes only a simple two-tier system. Two years after Edison and uncorroborated by any dated 2008-2011 document; presented as a genuine, unresolved tension rather than a settled answer - see docs/research/edison-rules.md.

sources.title: Yugipedia (then "Yu-Gi-Oh! Wiki"), "Forum:Chain Resolution and Priority" (posted/answered 2009-06-10/11)
sources.notes: A period ("Yu-Gi-Oh! Ruling Queries") community Q&A thread, dated via wikitext timestamps to 2009-06-10 23:07 UTC (question) and 2009-06-11 04:54 UTC (answer, confirmed correct), ~10.5 months before Edison. States explicitly: the turn player may use priority to activate an Ignition Effect as Chain Link 1 only "if the Chain ends with the Turn Player Special Summoning a monster" - if not, only Spell-Speed-2-or-higher priority is available, not Ignition. The clearest single period statement located for the "gate = Summon only, not any chain-end" finding in docs/research/edison-rules.md #1.

sources.title: Yugipedia, three "Yu-Gi-Oh! Ruling Queries" community forum threads on Ignition Effect Priority, dated March-July 2010 (bracketing Edison)
sources.notes: Three separate, genuinely-dated period threads, all framing the immediate "activate before the opponent can respond" Ignition Effect window around a Summon specifically, none describing a broader "any chain resolved" gate: "Forum:Costs_and_Priority" (2010-03-07, The Big Saturn example), "Forum:Priority...." (2010-03-12, Red-Eyes Darkness Metal Dragon/Blue-Eyes example, last edit 2010-03-12), and this page, "Forum:Ignition_Effect" (question 2010-03-24, last edit 2010-03-25) - the last one only three weeks before SJC Edison (2010-04-24). A fourth, "Forum:About_priority" (2010-07-14/16, three months after Edison), corroborates the same Summon-framing with two more worked examples (Batteryman Fuel Cell, Destiny End Dragoon).

sources.title: Yugipedia, "Forum:Sangan and Priority" (2010-10-01)
sources.notes: A period ruling thread (five months after Edison) confirming the flip side of the Summon gate with a real tournament-relevant Synchro Summon combo: a Summon that itself triggers a Mandatory Trigger Effect at the same moment (Sangan used as Synchro Material) does NOT grant Ignition Effect Priority on the resulting monster - "Priority is [automatically] passed to the opponent if the Mandatory Trigger Effect of a monster is activated at the moment a monster is summoned" - i.e. confirms the gate is specifically "a Summon that does not itself start a chain", not Summons in general.

sources.title: Yugipedia, "Card Rulings:Destiny HERO - Malicious", "OCG Rulings" section (citing Konami's official OCG rulings-FAQ database)
sources.notes: Cites a Konami OCG FAQ entry (yugioh.faq.konami.jp, itself unarchived/unretrievable - the underlying primary document remains a gap) stating that when Malicious is discarded to the GY by Foolish Burial/Armageddon Knight (a card effect, not a Summon), the turn player CANNOT use Priority to activate its Ignition Effect - the exact negative case (non-Summon chain-end) that isolates the gate this project's research turns on, using the exact card the task's research lead named. Labeled "OCG Rulings" by Yugipedia; treated here as consistent-with rather than proof-of the equivalent TCG rule, corroborated independently by TCG-specific community sources.

sources.title: Pojo.com Forums, "Rulebook Change for 0 vs 0 ATK monsters" (posted 2011-03-08 by Konami TCG Judge Program Manager "purity_reloaded")
sources.notes: The precise, dated (2011-03-08) primary-adjacent announcement of the 0-ATK rulebook change, posted by a self-identified Konami TCG "Judge Manager": "There has been an important change made to the latest version of the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG Official Rulebook, which is included with the Structure Deck: Dragunity Legion. The current version is listed as Version 7.2... 0 ATK monsters - Monsters with 0 ATK cannot destroy anything by battle. If two Attack Position monsters with 0 ATK battle each other, neither monster is destroyed." Replying to "I thought this was already true?": "Not until something was changed in the rulebook, it wasn't. At least for the TCG." This is also the exact source edisonformat.com itself cites for its own claim. Confirms both the exact wording and the exact date/product tying the change to the real world.

sources.title: Yugipedia, "Dragunity Legion Structure Deck" set-info page
sources.notes: Gives the TCG regional street dates for the structure deck Rulebook Version 7.2 was packaged with: North America 2011-03-08, other TCG territories 2011-03-03/04 - used to pin the 0-ATK rulebook change to on or shortly before this date, ~10.5 months after SJC Edison (2010-04-24), not the ~13-months-later date an earlier, mislabeled citation in this project implied.

sources.title: EdisonFormat.net, "Ignition-Priority" rules compendium page
sources.notes: A second, independently-authored (different domain/site from edisonformat.com) modern community reconstruction of the same Summon-gated, location-unrestricted Ignition Effect Priority rule, using a different worked example (Vorse Raider Normal Summoned, Plaguespreader Zombie's Ignition Effect activated from the GY immediately after). Not itself period evidence, but independent corroboration-in-shape of the period forum sources this project treats as primary for this question.
